newsitem.title: USA: French study questions cause of "mad cow" disease.
newsitem.headline: French study questions cause of "mad cow" disease.

text.p: A French study being published this week raises questions about the theory that "mad cow" disease is caused by a bizarre form of a protein, scientists said on Thursday.
Scientists have been split about whether an as-yet-undetected virus causes the disease or whether it is caused by a piece of mutated protein called a prion.
The finding, due to appear on Friday in the journal Science, deals a blow to the prion theory.

The report, by Corrine Lasmezas, Dominique Dormont and other researchers in Fontenay-aux-Roses, does not have any immediate impact on public health but may help scientists decipher the mysterious disease in the long term.
Many scientists fear mad cow disease can cross species barriers, spreading to humans and causing a form of the lethal neurological disorder Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease (CJD)

"There's a huge controversy over what the nature of the (infectious) agent is, embodied by this very radical idea that it's a protein prion," Robert Rohwer, an expert on CJD at the Baltimore Veterans Affairs medical research services, told Reuters. Rohwer himself is not a proponent of the prion theory.
The French researchers took tissue from cow brains containing bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE), as mad cow disease is formally known. They injected the tissue into mice.

All the mice developed neurological illness. But not all of them displayed the telltale amyloid -- an abnormal accumulation of the prion protein Rohwer described as "insoluble gunk" in the brain -- that would be expected if the abnormal prion was the infectious agent.
The team did several more generations of experiments, taking tissue from the dead diseased mice and infected a new set, and again they did not always find the amyloid "gunk."
That makes it less likely the abnormal prion theory is responsible for the disease, said Rohwer, commenting by telephone on the French research.
If the finding is confirmed by other labs, it makes it much more likely that a virus causes the disease.
